sources.title: Mathematics of Bioinformatics: Theory, Methods and Applications
sources.venue: John Wiley and Sons, Wiley Series in Bioinformatics. ISBN 978-0-470-40443-0. Cited in Version I as 'Theory, Practice, and Applications', the title used by the Nova Southeastern University listing
sources.access_status: Carried forward from Version I's bibliography, where it is the stated origin of the matrix formulation. Publication details independently confirmed by web search 2026-09-05; full text not consulted in this session.
supports: Version I's method of recording a Punnett grid as a matrix and raising it to a power
The diagonalisation approach used throughout Part I
does_not_establish: That a square operator is the correct representation of random mating
Any result derived in Parts III to VI

sources.title: Principles of Population Genetics
sources.access_status: Carried forward from Version I's bibliography, where it is the stated source of the Hardy-Weinberg allele-frequency formulas. Publication details independently confirmed by web search 2026-09-05; full text not consulted in this session.
supports: The Hardy-Weinberg genotype-frequency relations used to convert ABO phenotype shares into allele frequencies
Standard population-genetic vocabulary used in Part IV
does_not_establish: That Hardy-Weinberg assumptions hold for any pooled worldwide sample
The exact-test construction of Section 11.3, which is separately cited

sources.title: Pearson Baccalaureate Biology Higher Level, 2nd edition
sources.access_status: Transcribed from Version I's bibliography as cited by the author; not independently re-verified in this session.
supports: Version I's biological denotations: dominance, recessiveness, genotype and phenotype
Punnett-square construction as taught at that level
does_not_establish: Molecular detail of the ABO, Rh or HBB systems

sources.title: Haese Further Mathematics HL
sources.access_status: Transcribed from Version I's bibliography as cited by the author; not independently re-verified in this session.
supports: The eigenvalue, eigenvector and diagonalisation procedures restated in Section 3
does_not_establish: Any claim about which operator is biologically appropriate

sources.title: Kognity 3.1.1: Chromosomes, genes and alleles; and sickle-cell disease material
sources.venue: Kognity online learning platform, retrieved June and July 2022
sources.access_status: Transcribed from Version I's bibliography as cited by the author. Subscription platform; content not re-checked in this session.
supports: Version I's account of homozygous and heterozygous genotypes
Version I's description of the HbA and HbS codon change and its consequence for haemoglobin
does_not_establish: Clinical detail of sickle-cell disease, for which a primary reference is cited separately

sources.organization: Froedtert and the Medical College of Wisconsin
sources.title: Sickle Cell Disease: Symptoms
sources.venue: Froedtert and the Medical College of Wisconsin, retrieved 24 June 2022
sources.access_status: Transcribed from Version I's bibliography. Source of a figure in Version I comparing normal and sickled red blood cells; that figure is cited here and not reproduced.
supports: Version I's illustration of red-blood-cell morphology in sickle-cell disease
does_not_establish: Any quantitative parameter used in this work

sources.title: Sickle-cell anemia: regional malaria cases and HbS allele frequency
sources.access_status: Transcribed from Version I's bibliography. Source of a figure in Version I mapping malaria incidence against HbS frequency; that figure is cited here and not reproduced.
supports: Version I's statement of a geographic association between malaria and HbS frequency
does_not_establish: A causal claim about heterozygote advantage, which requires primary evidence
Any allele frequency used in a calculation

sources.title: Rh Blood Group System
sources.access_status: Transcribed from Version I's bibliography as cited by the author; not independently re-verified in this session.
supports: Version I's simplified dominant D / recessive d model of the Rh locus
The one-quarter Rh-negative outcome for two Dd parents
does_not_establish: Full RHD and RHCE variation, which the simplified model omits

sources.title: Blood Types: Revealing ABO Groups' Global Impact and Importance
sources.access_status: Transcribed from Version I's bibliography. This is a secondary summary, not a primary population survey, and it is the stated origin of the ABO phenotype percentages that drive Version I's coverage figures.
supports: Version I's worldwide ABO phenotype shares of approximately O 44%, A 42%, B 10%, AB 4%
does_not_establish: A sampling frame, sample size, or uncertainty for those percentages
That the pooled worldwide figures describe any single Hardy-Weinberg population

sources.title: Chart: How Blood Type Prevalence Varies Around the World
sources.access_status: Transcribed from Version I's bibliography. Secondary aggregator; it is the stated origin of the Rh phenotype split used in Version I's joint calculation.
supports: Version I's Rh-positive 93% and Rh-negative 7% phenotype split
does_not_establish: A sampling frame or uncertainty for that split
That a single global Rh frequency applies to any specific population

sources.title: Blood type
sources.access_status: Transcribed from Version I's bibliography. Tertiary source, used in Version I for orientation rather than for a quantitative input.
supports: Version I's general description of ABO codominance and O recessiveness
does_not_establish: Any frequency, molecular detail, or clinical claim relied upon here

sources.title: How long is a generation? Science provides an answer
sources.venue: International Society of Genetic Genealogy Wiki, 16 November 2016
sources.access_status: Transcribed from Version I's bibliography as cited by the author; not independently re-verified in this session.
supports: Version I's use of roughly 25 years as an average generation interval when converting generation counts into calendar years
does_not_establish: That a fixed generation interval applies across populations or eras
The calendar-year projections in Version I's conclusion, which Result 4.2 supersedes on separate grounds

sources.title: Desmos graphing calculator
sources.access_status: Transcribed from Version I's bibliography as cited by the author.
supports: The tool used to plot Version I's genotype-decay curves
does_not_establish: Any numerical result; the figures in this unified document are regenerated from retained output
